result:
I fixed the plan for its one blocking finding and applied the deferred items that belong in acceptance criteria. `plan-state render` exits 0, and `plan-state check` prints nothing and exits 0. `render` changed nothing beyond my edits, the `## Audit record` section is untouched, and nothing is committed. The diff is +27/−9 lines, all in one file.

## Blocking finding R2-B1 (task-round): the CRLF test cannot pass on this machine
On Git Bash, gawk reads the plan in text mode and drops the CR, so a CRLF plan comes out all-LF. The fix is the reconciliation's R.1 and R.2:

- **R.1:** In the `emit()` sketch, the awk call is now `awk -v BINMODE=3 -v MODE=emit …`. A comment above it gives the reason: MSYS gawk drops the CR, `BINMODE=3` keeps the bytes, and other awks treat it as an unused variable. It is on the emit call only.
  - I checked this on a CRLF copy of this plan with a patched copy of the script. Without the change, `render` left 0 of 1024 CRs; with it, all 1024 stayed, under both sh and dash.
- **R.2:** The CRLF acceptance criterion now says how to check the bytes:
  - **Every line ends in CR:** `tr -cd '\r' < "$f" | wc -c` must equal `wc -l < "$f"`, compared with `-eq`.
  - **The inserted line:** write it out with `head -n K | tail -n 1` and compare it with `cmp` to a file written by `printf 'review_rounds: 1\r\n'`.
  - **Don't use:** plain `awk`, `sed`, `grep` or `has`, since all four drop the CR here.

  One addition beyond the reconciliation's wording: in Git Bash, `$(...)` strips a trailing CR and LF together. So capturing the line in a variable and comparing it to a `printf` string would fail even when the file is correct. I tested this, which is why the criterion uses files and `cmp`. That still compares against a `printf`-built value, as R.2 asks, and it also says not to hold the line in `$(...)`.

## Deferred items applied (all in acceptance criteria)
- **D.1 (D6), task-preflight-declared:** the Mixed case now states its fixture: `task-d` depends on `task-x` and `task-s`; `task-s` is a root.
- **D.2 (D7), task-preflight-declared:** every "prints no line" case now also requires exit 0. That covers Siblings with the dependency added, Grand-ancestor, and P4 with `task-w` done or with `task-x` depending on `task-w`.
- **D.3 (R2-D8), task-preflight-edit:** new case. The rename text cites `lib/greet.sh:4`, which is absent and undeclared. Expected: exit 1, with the P1 warning printed before the P3 error. This is the only case that shows whether output is ordered by check id or with errors first.
- **E (R2-D9), task-preflight-edit:** the EU-A criterion is now a command the implementer runs:
  - For each of `mawk` and `busybox` that is installed, run the whole suite with an `awk` shim first on PATH. With each one present, it must end `RESULT: N passed, 0 failed`.
  - The DONE report names which awks ran and has one `NOTE:` per missing awk.
  - A `NOTE:` outcome leaves EU-A open.

  The reconciliation left a choice here. I took option (b), the full-suite run. Option (a) also required editing the audit record, which you told me to leave alone.

## Not applied
These are recommended but not acceptance-criteria items, so they stay out:
- R.3 (rewrite the whole `review_rounds` line)
- R.4 (`-v CAP` on the `check` awk call)
- P.1–P.5 (fixes to the preflight awk sketches)

F and the "say so in the record" part of E would change the audit record, which you said to keep as it is. So the record still describes P, D and E as proposed, not applied.
